en.name: Rice wine (cooking)
en.summary: Chinese cooking rice wines — 米酒, Shaoxing, huadiao — are brewed or fortified alcohol at roughly 15 to 20 percent by volume, and alcohol at that strength is a preservation barrier in its own right. There is no published home shelf life, so this record gives the rule rather than inventing a number: keep it capped, cool and dark, and it does not need the fridge.
en.pantry: The cupboard is the right place: capped, upright, cool and dark, away from the hob. Alcohol at this strength controls microbial growth the way acidification and salt do in other foods, which is why no refrigeration is required. It does not spoil in the ordinary sense; what it does is oxidise, going flat and slightly sharp over a long spell with the bottle open. No agency publishes a home shelf life for Chinese cooking wine, so none is given here rather than one being invented. Cooking wines sold with salt added to sidestep liquor licensing behave the same way.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is not needed and will not stop the oxidation that dulls an opened bottle — the cap and the dark do more than the cold. There is no published refrigerated timeline either, so there is nothing to offer in place of the rule. If you cook with a drinking rice wine that you also pour at the table, judge it as a drink rather than as a seasoning, which is a much shorter clock.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for cooking rice wine and no reason to freeze it. At this alcohol strength it will not freeze solid in a domestic freezer, and the alcohol is already doing the preserving. Freezer space is better spent on something perishable.
spoilage: A flat, sherry-like or vinegary smell where there was a clean grain one
A colour that has darkened noticeably since the bottle was opened
Cloudiness or floating matter in a bottle that was clear
Mould around the neck or cap, usually in dried residue
tips: Cap it tightly — air, not time, is what flattens an opened bottle.
Keep it away from the hob; heat ages an open bottle fastest.
Decant into a smaller bottle once it is half empty to cut down on air.
Judge it by smell: a flat, sharp bottle will make a flat, sharp dish.

faq.q: Does cooking rice wine need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. At roughly 15 to 20 percent alcohol it preserves itself. Keep it capped in a cool dark cupboard.

faq.q: How long does rice wine last after opening?
faq.a: No agency publishes a home shelf life, so no number is given. Judge it by smell and colour — it flattens gradually rather than spoiling.

faq.q: Does salted cooking wine keep differently?
faq.a: No. Salt is added to sidestep liquor licensing, and the bottle behaves the same way: cool, dark, capped.
There is no timeline and no reason to. It will not freeze solid at this alcohol strength.

zh.name: 料理米酒
zh.summary: 中式料理用酒——米酒、紹興、花雕——是酒精濃度約 15 到 20% 的釀造或強化酒，而這個濃度的酒精本身就是一道保存屏障。目前沒有已發表的家庭保存期限，所以本篇給的是規則而不是憑空捏造的數字：蓋緊、陰涼、避光，而且不需要冰箱。
zh.pantry: 櫥櫃就是對的位置：蓋緊、直立、陰涼、避光、遠離爐火。這個濃度的酒精控制微生物生長的方式，就像其他食品靠酸化和鹽一樣，所以不需要冷藏。它不會以一般意義上的方式腐敗；它會做的是氧化——開瓶後放久會變扁、帶點刺酸。沒有機構公布中式料理酒的家庭保存期限，所以這裡寧可不給，也不憑空捏造。為了避開酒類販售規範而加鹽的料理酒，行為也完全相同。
zh.fridge: 不需要冷藏，冷藏也擋不住讓開瓶酒變鈍的氧化——蓋子和避光比低溫有用。冷藏同樣沒有已發表的期限，所以也沒有數字可以取代這條規則。如果你用的是自己也會斟來喝的米酒，那就以飲品的標準判斷它，而那是短得多的時鐘。
zh.freezer: 料理米酒沒有冷凍期限，也沒有冷凍的理由。這個酒精濃度在家用冷凍庫不會凍硬，而酒精本來就在做保存的工作。冷凍庫的空間留給易腐食材比較划算。
spoilage: 原本乾淨的穀物酒香變成扁平的雪莉味或醋味
顏色比剛開瓶時明顯變深
原本清澈的瓶子變濁或出現漂浮物
瓶口或瓶蓋的乾漬處長霉
tips: 蓋緊——讓開瓶酒變扁的是空氣，不是時間。
遠離爐火；高溫讓開瓶後的酒老化最快。
喝到剩一半時換小瓶裝，減少瓶內空氣。
用氣味判斷：一瓶扁平刺酸的酒，只會煮出扁平刺酸的菜。

faq.a: 不用。酒精濃度約 15 到 20%，它能自我保存。蓋緊放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃即可。

faq.q: 料理米酒開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 沒有機構公布家庭保存期限，所以這裡不給數字。請用氣味和顏色判斷——它是逐漸變扁，而不是腐敗。

faq.q: 加鹽的料理酒保存方式不同嗎？
faq.a: 不同之處只在標示。加鹽是為了避開酒類販售規範，保存方式完全一樣：陰涼、避光、蓋緊。
沒有對應期限，也沒有理由。這個酒精濃度根本凍不硬。
